items.title: Murnaghan stability for Kronecker coefficients
items.statement: Fix partitions alpha, beta, gamma. Put m(gamma):=max{|alpha|+alpha_1, |beta|+beta_1, |gamma|+gamma_1} and, for n >= m(gamma), let g_n(alpha,beta,gamma):=g^{gamma[n]}_{alpha[n],beta[n]} be the multiplicity of the Specht module V_{gamma[n]} in V_{alpha[n]} (x) V_{beta[n]}; set g_n(alpha,beta,gamma):=0 for n<m(gamma). Then the sequence n |-> g_n(alpha,beta,gamma) is eventually constant. More precisely there is a finite set S(alpha,beta) of partitions and nonnegative integers bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} for gamma in S(alpha,beta), with bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}:=0 for gamma not in S(alpha,beta), such that g_n(alpha,beta,gamma)=bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} for all sufficiently large n and every partition gamma. No explicit bound on the stable rank is asserted here (the sharp global bound is a separate claim).
items.strategy: FI-module route of Church-Ellenberg-Farb. By CEF Proposition 3.4.1 the assignments V(alpha)_n:=V_{alpha[n]} for n>=|alpha|+alpha_1 and V(alpha)_n:=0 below define a finitely generated FI-module. By CEF Proposition 2.3.6 the tensor product V(alpha)(x)V(alpha) is finitely generated and its value in rank n is V_{alpha[n]} (x) V_{beta[n]}. CEF Theorem 1.13 states that a finitely generated FI-module over a field of characteristic 0 is uniformly representation stable: there is a finite set of partitions nu and fixed multiplicities c_nu such that the rank-n value is the direct sum of c_nu copies of V(nu)_n for all n in a stable range. Restricting to the single irreducible family nu=gamma and reading off multiplicities gives the eventual constancy of n |-> g_n(alpha,beta,gamma); the finiteness of the support is the finiteness of the constituent list. All inputs are the in-run suppliers named in deps; the argument is choice-free.
items.axiom_use: None: the proof is finite-dimensional representation theory over a characteristic-zero field plus the choice-free FI-module finite-generation machinery of the cited suppliers.

items.title: The reduced (stable) Kronecker coefficient
items.statement: For partitions alpha, beta, gamma define the reduced (stable) Kronecker coefficient bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} to be the eventual value of the padded sequence n |-> g_n(alpha,beta,gamma) furnished by the Murnaghan stability theorem; equivalently bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} := lim_{n to infinity} g^{gamma[n]}_{alpha[n],beta[n]}, where the sequence is defined for n>=max{|alpha|+alpha_1,|beta|+beta_1,|gamma|+gamma_1} and set to 0 below. Well-definedness is exactly the Murnaghan stability theorem. Two immediate conventions: bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}=bar-g^gamma_{beta,alpha} (commutativity of the tensor product), and for fixed alpha,beta only finitely many gamma have bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} nonzero. Values used later and verified in the source's introduction for alpha=beta=(2): bar-g^{(2)}_{(2),(2)}=2 and bar-g^{(4)}_{(2),(2)}=1.
items.strategy: Well-definedness is the preceding theorem: the eventual constant of an eventually constant sequence of nonnegative integers is a unique nonnegative integer, no choice is involved. The symmetry in alpha,beta is the commutativity of the tensor product of representations. The two displayed values are read from the source's introduction's product table and are not used as logical inputs.

items.title: The padded sequence completion, the operators U_n and V, and stab(alpha,beta)
items.statement: Let alpha=(alpha_1,...,alpha_k) be a partition and n>=0; the padded sequence is alpha[n]:=(n-|alpha|,alpha_1,...,alpha_k). For an arbitrary finite sequence of integers mu=(mu_1,...,mu_m) define s_mu by the Jacobi-Trudi determinant det(h_{mu_j+i-j})_{1<=i,j<=m} with h_k=0 for k<0, as in the source; every such determinant is either 0 or +-1 times a Schur function. Define Z-linear endomorphisms of the ring of symmetric functions by U_n(s_lambda):=s_{lambda[n]} and V(s_lambda):=s_{lambda+(1)} on the Schur basis, extended linearly. Finally, for partitions alpha,beta define stab(alpha,beta) to be the least n_0>=0 such that s_{alpha[n_0+k]}*s_{beta[n_0+k]}=V^k(s_{alpha[n_0]}*s_{beta[n_0]}) as elements of the symmetric function ring for all k>0, where * is the internal product; stab(alpha,beta) is not shown to exist by this definition alone (its existence and value are the sharp global threshold theorem).
items.strategy: U_n and V are well-defined by linear extension from the Schur basis, which is a Z-basis. The Jacobi-Trudi completion is well-defined by the published Jacobi-Trudi identities with the convention h_k=0 for k<0, and the sign statement is the standard column-permutation computation. The definition of stab(alpha,beta) only records the source's convention; no existence statement is claimed here.
items.axiom_use: None: the Jacobi-Trudi completion and the linear extensions are Z-linear algebra on the free abelian group on partitions.

items.title: Lambda-ring specializations of symmetric functions and the series sigma
items.statement: Work in the algebra of symmetric functions over Q in an alphabet X, in which the power sums p_1,p_2,... are algebraically independent generators. A specialization is an algebra homomorphism f |-> f[A] to a commutative Q-algebra; it is determined by the sequence (p_k[A])_{k>=1}, and conversely every sequence of values gives one. For specializations A,B, a scalar z and the symbols +, product and -, define p_k[A+B]:=p_k[A]+p_k[B], p_k[-A]:=-p_k[A], p_k[zA]:=zp_k[A] and p_k[AB]:=p_k[A]p_k[B], and write f[A+B], f[-A], f[AB], f[zA] for the images of f under the corresponding homomorphisms. Define X^perp to be the specialization with f[X^perp]:=f^perp for all f, where f^perp denotes the adjoint of multiplication by f with respect to the Hall inner product. Define the series sigma[X]:=sum_{n>=0} h_n[X].
items.strategy: Existence and uniqueness of a specialization with prescribed p_k-values is the universal property of the polynomial ring Q[p_1,p_2,...]: the p_k are algebraically independent, so a homomorphism is specified by arbitrary images of the p_k and such a homomorphism exists. The operations on specializations are defined on the p_k and extended multiplicatively, again by the universal property. The adjoint f^perp of multiplication by f exists and is unique because the Hall form is nondegenerate and each graded piece of the symmetric function ring is finite dimensional (the Schur functions are an orthonormal basis). No choice is used.
items.axiom_use: None: algebraic independence of the power sums over Q and finite-dimensional nondegenerate bilinear algebra.

items.title: Schur functions on sums and products of alphabets
items.statement: For all partitions lambda,mu,nu and all specializations A,B: (a) s_lambda[A+B] = sum_{mu,nu} c^lambda_{mu,nu} s_mu[A] s_nu[B], the sum over pairs with |mu|+|nu|=|lambda|; (b) s_lambda[AB] = sum_{mu,nu} g^lambda_{mu,nu} s_mu[A] s_nu[B], the sum over pairs with |mu|=|nu|=|lambda|, where g^lambda_{mu,nu} is the ordinary Kronecker coefficient. Both sums are finite.
items.strategy: (a) By the Jacobi-Trudi presentation and p_k[A+B]=p_k[A]+p_k[B] the complete homogeneous functions satisfy h_m[A+B]=sum_{i+j=m} h_i[A] h_j[B]; expanding the Jacobi-Trudi determinant of s_lambda[A+B] with this convolution and using the LR rule for products of complete homogeneous functions gives the stated expansion (equivalently, this is the coproduct form of the LR rule). (b) Both sides are multiplicative in the two alphabets and are Q-bilinear; the identity is the classical plethysm expansion of a Schur function in a product of alphabets, equivalent to the character statement that S^lambda(V (x) W) decomposes with multiplicities g^lambda_{mu,nu}. In the lambda-ring formalism of the source, (b) is exactly the displayed identity s_lambda[XY]=sum g_{lambda,mu,nu}s_mu[X]s_nu[Y].

items.title: The sigma series: Cauchy identity, adjunction and reproducing kernel
items.statement: Let sigma[X]=sum_{n>=0}h_n[X]. (1) sigma[X]=prod_{x in X}(1-x)^{-1} and sigma[-X]=prod_{x in X}(1-x); in particular sigma[t]=(1-t)^{-1} and sigma[-t]=1-t for a scalar t. (2) sigma[A+B]=sigma[A]sigma[B] and sigma[zA]=sigma[A] restricted to z (i.e. sigma[A+B] is multiplicative over sums of specializations). (3) Cauchy identity: sigma[XY]=sum_lambda s_lambda[X]s_lambda[Y]. (4) For every specialization A the operator sigma[AX^perp] is the adjoint of multiplication by sigma[AX]: sigma[AX^perp]f[X]=f[X+A] for all f. (5) Reproducing kernel: <sigma[AX] | f[X]>_X = f[A] for all f.
items.strategy: (1) is the elementary product formula for the generating function of complete homogeneous functions, together with p_k[-A]=-p_k[A]; (2) is immediate from (1) and the multiplicativity p_k[AB]=p_k[A]p_k[B]. (3) is Cauchy's identity, obtained by expanding prod_{x,y}(1-xy)^{-1} as a geometric series and collecting monomials by Schur functions via the bialternant/Schur expansion of the complete homogeneous functions. For (4) and (5): by Cauchy, sigma[AX]=sum_rho s_rho[A]s_rho[X], so multiplication by sigma[AX] is the operator sum_rho s_rho[A](multiplication by s_rho); for f=s_lambda and any g, <sigma[AX^perp]s_lambda,g>=<s_lambda,sigma[AX]g>=sum_rho s_rho[A]<s_lambda,s_rho g>=sum_rho s_rho[A] c^lambda_{rho,mu}=[s_mu]s_lambda[X+A] using the coproduct identity (a) of the previous lemma and orthonormality of the Schur basis. Taking g=s_mu shows (4); (5) is its equivalent dual form (evaluate on f=s_lambda and expand).

items.title: Vertex-operator generating series for the padded Schur functions
items.statement: Let alpha be a partition and t a formal variable. With the Jacobi-Trudi convention of the first definition item for the integer sequences alpha[n]=(n-|alpha|,alpha_1,alpha_2,...), one has the identity of formal Laurent series with coefficients in the symmetric function ring: sum_{n in Z} s_{alpha[n]}[X] t^n = sigma[tX] . s_alpha[tX - 1] = t^{|alpha|} . sigma[tX] . s_alpha[X - t^{-1}], where s_alpha[tX-1] is evaluated through the specialization p_k |-> t^k p_k[X] - 1 and s_alpha[X-t^{-1}] through p_k |-> p_k[X]-t^{-k}. Equivalently, sum_{n in Z} s_{alpha[n]}[X]t^n = sigma[tX] sum_{mu: alpha/mu a vertical strip} (-1)^{|alpha|-|mu|} t^{|mu|} s_mu[X]. (This is the growth paper's identity (6) p. 7, displayed there as t^{|alpha|}Gamma(t|X)s_alpha[X] = sigma[tX]s_alpha[tX-1].)
items.strategy: Two ingredients, both available locally. (a) The coproduct identity s_alpha[A+B]=sum_{mu,nu}c^alpha_{mu,nu}s_mu[A]s_nu[B] of the previous lemma, applied to the negative of a one-point alphabet: the negative-alphabet rule s_nu[-A]=(-1)^{|nu|}s_{nu'}[A] is a direct consequence of the involution omega (p_k |-> (-1)^{k-1}p_k) in the power-sum basis, so s_nu[-{1}] equals (-1)^{|nu|} when nu is a single column and 0 otherwise; hence s_alpha[tX-1]=sum_{mu: alpha/mu a vertical strip}(-1)^{|alpha|-|mu|}s_mu[tX], equivalently s_alpha[X-t^{-1}]=sum_{mu: alpha/mu a vertical strip}(-t^{-1})^{|alpha|-|mu|}s_mu[X]. (b) The Pieri rule h_m s_mu=sum_{nu: nu/mu a horizontal strip of size m}s_nu. The right-hand side t^{|alpha|}sigma[tX]s_alpha[X-t^{-1}] is then exactly the sum over pairs (m,mu) of (-1)^{|alpha|-|mu|}h_m s_mu t^{m+|mu|}; collecting the coefficient of t^n and applying the Pieri rule produces the signed sum over pairs mu subset nu with alpha/mu a vertical strip and nu/mu a horizontal strip of size n-|mu|, of (-1)^{|alpha|-|mu|}s_nu. The Jacobi-Trudi determinant of the integer sequence alpha[n], expanded along its first row, is precisely this signed chain sum; this identifies the coefficient of t^n with s_{alpha[n]}[X] for every n. The identity is the classical Bernstein/Jing vertex-operator formula (source: growth paper section 2.4 formula (6) p. 7, and the Bernstein operators of Macdonald I.5 Example 29).

items.title: Brion's formula and the symmetric Cauchy-type identity for reduced Kronecker coefficients
items.statement: For all partitions alpha,beta,gamma: bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} = < s_alpha[X] s_beta[Y] | sigma[XY] s_gamma[XY+X+Y] >_{X,Y}, the inner product being the extension of the Hall inner product to symmetric functions in two alphabets X,Y. Equivalently, introducing a third alphabet Z, sum_{alpha,beta,gamma} bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} s_alpha[X]s_beta[Y]s_gamma[Z] = sigma[XYZ+XY+XZ+YZ], the symmetric Cauchy-type identity of the source.
items.strategy: Follow the complete proof of the source's Proposition 3.2. For fixed gamma the padded coefficient g_{alpha[n],beta[n],gamma[n]} equals <s_{gamma[n]}[XY] | s_{alpha[n]}[X] s_{beta[n]}[Y]>_{X,Y} by the coproduct identity (the Schur functions s_mu[X]s_nu[Y] are orthonormal and s_mu[XY] expands as sum_{alpha,beta} g^mu_{alpha,beta} s_alpha[X]s_beta[Y]). Form the generating series G(t):=sum_n g_{alpha[n],beta[n],gamma[n]}t^n and substitute the vertex-operator series for both factors; applying the adjoint identities sigma[AX^perp]f=f[X+A] (with A=1) and the reproducing kernel turns G(t) into (1-t)^{-1}P(t) with P(t) a polynomial in t (the truncation is legitimate because sigma[tXY] is homogeneous of total degree 2k in X,Y while the other factor has bounded X-degree). A sequence is eventually constant if and only if its generating series has the form P(t)/(1-t) with P a polynomial, and then the stable value is P(1) (the source's Lemma 3.3). Substituting t=1 in P(t) gives Brion's formula; the three-alphabet identity follows by taking scalar products with s_gamma[Z] and using the reproducing kernel <sigma[AZ]|s_gamma[Z]>=s_gamma[A] with A=XY+X+Y. The eventual value computed is bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} by the definition of the reduced coefficient.
items.axiom_use: None: the proof uses the lambda-ring calculus, Cauchy's identity and formal power series in one variable over a characteristic-zero algebra.

items.title: Threefold Schur coefficients
items.statement: For partitions delta,a,b,c with |delta|=|a|+|b|+|c| define the threefold Schur coefficient c^delta_{a,b,c}:=[s_delta] s_a s_b s_c, the coefficient of s_delta in the ordinary product of the three Schur functions. These are nonnegative integers, they are symmetric in a,b,c, and they satisfy the iterated Littlewood-Richardson identity c^delta_{a,b,c}=sum_phi c^phi_{a,b} c^delta_{phi,c}=sum_psi c^psi_{a,c}c^delta_{psi,b}, the sums over partitions phi (respectively psi) of |a|+|b| (respectively |a|+|c|). Equivalently c^delta_{a,b,c}=<s_a s_b s_c | s_delta>.
items.strategy: Nonnegativity and the symmetry in a,b,c are immediate from the definition and commutativity of the product. The iterated identity is the associativity of the Schur product: s_as_bs_c = (s_as_b)s_c = sum_phi c^phi_{a,b}s_phi s_c = sum_{phi,delta}c^phi_{a,b}c^delta_{phi,c}s_delta, compared with the definition. The inner-product form is orthonormality of the Schur basis.

items.title: Nonnegative expansion of a reduced Kronecker coefficient
items.statement: For all partitions alpha,beta,gamma one has the finite nonnegative expansion bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} = sum_{mu,lambda,eta,rho,theta,pi} c^gamma_{mu,theta,pi} c^alpha_{rho,lambda,theta} c^beta_{rho,eta,pi} g^mu_{lambda,eta}, the sum over all six-tuples of partitions (only finitely many summands are nonzero), where the c's are threefold Schur coefficients and the g's are ordinary Kronecker coefficients. Consequences: (i) bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}>0 if and only if there exist partitions mu,lambda,eta,rho,theta,pi with c^gamma_{mu,theta,pi}, c^alpha_{rho,lambda,theta}, c^beta_{rho,eta,pi} and g^mu_{lambda,eta} all positive; (ii) for every nonzero summand the degree equations |alpha|=|rho|+|lambda|+|theta|, |beta|=|rho|+|eta|+|pi|, |gamma|=|mu|+|theta|+|pi| and |mu|=|lambda|=|eta| hold; (iii) for fixed alpha,beta the index set is finite because rho,lambda,theta are contained in alpha, rho,eta,pi in beta, and |mu|=|lambda|. All summands are nonnegative integers, so no cancellation occurs.
items.strategy: Expand Brion's formula in the two alphabets X,Y: sigma[XY] = sum_rho s_rho[X]s_rho[Y] by Cauchy, and s_gamma[XY+X+Y] = sum_{mu,nu} c^gamma_{mu,nu} s_mu[XY] s_nu[X+Y] by the coproduct identity, then s_mu[XY] = sum_{lambda,eta} g^mu_{lambda,eta} s_lambda[X]s_eta[Y] and s_nu[X+Y] = sum_{theta,pi} c^nu_{theta,pi}s_theta[X]s_pi[Y] by the coproduct and plethysm identities. The right-hand side becomes sum c^gamma_{mu,nu} c^nu_{theta,pi} g^mu_{lambda,eta} s_rho s_lambda s_theta[X] s_rho s_eta s_pi[Y]; the coefficient of s_alpha[X]s_beta[Y] is sum over rho,lambda,theta of c^alpha_{rho,lambda,theta} (respectively rho,eta,pi) times the rest. Using the iterated identity sum_nu c^gamma_{mu,nu}c^nu_{theta,pi}=c^gamma_{mu,theta,pi} gives the displayed formula. Consequences (i),(ii) are the positivity and degree bookkeeping of the individual summands (the supports of threefold coefficients and of g are governed by containment and total degree). This proves the source's Lemma 2.1 in the derived index pattern; the source's displayed equality (8) prints a third-factor index set that is a typographical variant of the same K_4 index pattern (the version proved here is the one used by the source's proof and by their if-and-only-if statement).
items.axiom_use: None: the expansion is an elementary computation in the lambda-ring with Cauchy's identity and the coproduct/plethysm identities; all coefficients are nonnegative integers.

items.title: Murnaghan-Littlewood: top-degree reduced coefficients are Littlewood-Richardson coefficients
items.statement: Let alpha,beta,gamma be partitions with |gamma|=|alpha|+|beta|. Then bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}=c^gamma_{alpha,beta}, the Littlewood-Richardson coefficient. In particular bar-g^{alpha+beta}_{alpha,beta}=c^{alpha+beta}_{alpha,beta}=1.
items.strategy: Apply the nonnegative expansion of the preceding lemma. For every nonzero summand the degree equations give |alpha|+|beta|-|gamma| = (|rho|+|lambda|+|theta|)+(|rho|+|eta|+|pi|)-(|mu|+|theta|+|pi|) = 2|rho|+|lambda|+|eta|-|mu| = 2|rho|+|mu|, using |lambda|=|eta|=|mu|. If |gamma|=|alpha|+|beta| then 2|rho|+|mu|=0, so rho=mu=empty; then |lambda|=|eta|=0, so lambda=eta=empty; hence c^alpha_{rho,lambda,theta}=c^alpha_{empty,empty,theta}=delta_{alpha,theta} and c^beta_{empty,empty,pi}=delta_{beta,pi}, and the six-fold sum collapses to the single summand g^empty_{empty,empty} c^gamma_{alpha,beta} = c^gamma_{alpha,beta}. For gamma=alpha+beta the LR coefficient equals 1: the Pieri/LR rule gives the unique Littlewood-Richardson tableau of shape (alpha+beta)/alpha whose row i is filled with i's.

items.title: The support of the reduced Kronecker coefficients satisfies the size triangle inequalities
items.statement: If bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}>0 then |alpha| <= |beta|+|gamma|, |beta| <= |alpha|+|gamma| and |gamma| <= |alpha|+|beta| (Murnaghan's inequalities). Hence the support Supp(alpha,beta) of the nonzero reduced coefficients with fixed alpha,beta lies in the triangle region of the weight lattice.
items.strategy: Take a nonzero summand of the nonnegative expansion and use its degree equations |alpha|=|rho|+|lambda|+|theta|, |beta|=|rho|+|eta|+|pi|, |gamma|=|mu|+|theta|+|pi| with |lambda|=|eta|=|mu|. Subtracting pairwise: |alpha|+|beta|-|gamma| = 2|rho|+|mu| >= 0; |alpha|+|gamma|-|beta| = |lambda|+2|theta|+|mu|-|eta| = 2|theta|+|mu| >= 0; |beta|+|gamma|-|alpha| = 2|pi|+|mu| >= 0. Each difference is a sum of nonnegative integers, giving the three inequalities for that summand, hence for their positive sum.

items.title: The Murnaghan expansion in the Jacobi-Trudi extension for all admissible ranks
items.statement: For all partitions alpha,beta and every n >= max{|alpha|+alpha_1, |beta|+beta_1}: s_{alpha[n]} * s_{beta[n]} = sum_gamma bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} s_{gamma[n]}, an identity in the symmetric function ring, where s_{gamma[n]} is the Jacobi-Trudi determinant attached to the integer sequence gamma[n] (zero or +-1 times a Schur function). Equivalently, for every n in that range and every partition gamma, g^{gamma[n]}_{alpha[n],beta[n]} = bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}. The range displayed is precisely the set of n for which alpha[n] and beta[n] are partitions.
items.strategy: Source route (Briand-Orellana-Rosas, Murnaghan Theorem p. 4 and Lemma 3.1 pp. 8-9): the expansion is Murnaghan's theorem in the Jacobi-Trudi extension. The two published proofs available for local adaptation are (i) Littlewood's identity s_{alpha[n]}*s_{beta[n]} = U_n R_{alpha,beta}, where R_{alpha,beta} = sum_{delta,epsilon,tau}((s_delta s_tau)^perp s_alpha)((s_epsilon s_tau)^perp s_beta)(s_delta * s_epsilon), combined with injectivity of U_n in degrees <= n/2 (BOR pp. 7-8, identity (9), attributed to Littlewood [Lit58] and reproduced in Butler-King 1973 Formula 6.1 and Scharf-Thibon-Wybourne 1993 Formula 8), and (ii) a vertex-operator argument comparing the generating series sum_n s_{alpha[n]}*s_{beta[n]}z^n on both sides, which equals (sum_n s_{alpha[n]}z^n)*(sum_m s_{beta[m]}z^m) and so should be evaluated with the vertex-operator series of the preceding lemma. Neither route is yet reduced to in-library items: route (i) requires the Littlewood identity, whose only available proofs (Littlewood's invariant theory, Brion's geometry, Thibon's vertex operators, partition-algebra proofs) have not been read to a locally checkable form, and route (ii) requires the *(X,Y)-compatibility of the internal product with the vertex-operator factorization, which is not yet established locally. This item is therefore recorded as escalated.
items.axiom_use: None intended; the missing input is the Littlewood identity or an equivalent all-rank argument.

items.title: The exact global stabilization threshold for a fixed Kronecker product
items.statement: For all partitions alpha,beta: stab(alpha,beta) = |alpha|+|beta|+alpha_1+beta_1. Equivalently, the whole Schur internal product s_{alpha[n]}*s_{beta[n]} equals its stable reduced expansion sum_gamma bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}s_{gamma[n]} (with the Jacobi-Trudi completion on the right) for every n >= |alpha|+|beta|+alpha_1+beta_1, and this is the least index from which the product is V-stable: the product at index N := |alpha|+|beta|+alpha_1+beta_1 is not equal to V of the product at index N-1, because the expansion at index N contains the term s_{gamma*[N]} for gamma* = alpha+beta, a Schur function whose first two parts are equal, while every element of the image of V is a combination of Schur functions with strictly greater first than second part. No sharpness of this global bound for an individual coefficient is claimed (see the companion counterexample).
items.strategy: Source route: Briand-Orellana-Rosas Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, pp. 8-9. (i) Support maximum: every nonzero summand of the nonnegative expansion satisfies |gamma|+gamma_1 <= |alpha|+|beta|+alpha_1+beta_1 - the chain is |gamma|+gamma_1 <= |mu|+mu_1+|theta|+theta_1+|pi|+pi_1 <= 2|mu|+|theta|+theta_1+|pi|+pi_1 = |lambda|+|theta|+theta_1+|eta|+|pi|+pi_1 <= |alpha|+alpha_1+|beta|+beta_1, using the threefold containment theta subset alpha, pi subset beta, the row bound gamma_1 <= mu_1+theta_1+pi_1 from the LR rule, mu_1 <= |mu|, |mu|=|lambda|=|eta| and |lambda|+|theta| <= |alpha|, |eta|+|pi| <= |beta|; combined with the top-degree lemma, which shows that gamma=alpha+beta attains the value |alpha|+|beta|+alpha_1+beta_1, this identifies max{|gamma|+gamma_1 : bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}>0} = |alpha|+|beta|+alpha_1+beta_1. (ii) Lemma 3.1 identifies stab(alpha,beta) with that maximum: the product at n=N has all gamma[N] partitions, so Murnaghan's expansion gives V-stability from N onwards, while V-stability fails from N-1: the expansion at index N exhibits the term s_{gamma*[N]} with gamma*=alpha+beta, whose first two parts are equal, and no Schur function with equal first two parts lies in the image of V (V(s_mu)=s_{mu+(1)} has first part strictly greater than its second). Step (i) is fully scaffolded above; step (ii) needs the all-admissible-rank Murnaghan expansion (the preceding item), which is recorded as escalated, so this theorem is escalated as well.

items.title: Murnaghan stability for alpha = beta = (2), ranks 4 to 9
items.statement: For alpha=beta=(2) the source's introduction displays s_{2,2}*s_{2,2}=s_4+s_{1,1,1,1}+s_{2,2}; s_{3,2}*s_{3,2}=s_5+s_{2,1,1,1}+s_{3,2}+s_{4,1}+s_{3,1,1}+s_{2,2,1}; s_{4,2}*s_{4,2}=s_6+s_{3,1,1,1}+2s_{4,2}+s_{5,1}+s_{4,1,1}+2s_{3,2,1}+s_{2,2,2}; s_{5,2}*s_{5,2}=s_7+s_{4,1,1,1}+2s_{5,2}+s_{6,1}+s_{5,1,1}+2s_{4,2,1}+s_{3,2,2}+s_{4,3}+s_{3,3,1}; s_{6,2}*s_{6,2}=s_8+s_{5,1,1,1}+2s_{6,2}+s_{7,1}+s_{6,1,1}+2s_{5,2,1}+s_{4,2,2}+s_{5,3}+s_{4,3,1}+s_{4,4}; s_{7,2}*s_{7,2}=s_9+s_{6,1,1,1}+2s_{7,2}+s_{8,1}+s_{7,1,1}+2s_{6,2,1}+s_{5,2,2}+s_{6,3}+s_{5,3,1}+s_{5,4}; and the stable row s_{bullet,2}*s_{bullet,2}=s_bullet+s_{bullet,1,1,1}+2s_{bullet,2}+s_{bullet,1}+s_{bullet,1,1}+2s_{bullet,2,1}+s_{bullet,2,2}+s_{bullet,3}+s_{bullet,3,1}+s_{bullet,4}. Consequently the reduced coefficients for the pair ((2),(2)) are bar-g^gamma_{(2),(2)} = 1,1,2,1,1,2,1,1,1,1 for gamma = empty, (1,1,1), (2), (1), (1,1), (2,1), (2,2), (3), (3,1), (4) respectively, and bar-g^gamma=0 for all other gamma; in particular bar-g^{(2)}_{(2),(2)}=2 and bar-g^{(4)}_{(2),(2)}=1. The displayed data also verify directly, for this pair, that the whole product is V-stable at rank 8 and not at rank 7: applying V (adding a box to the first row of every Schur function) to the rank-8 expansion s_{6,2}*s_{6,2} reproduces the rank-9 expansion s_{7,2}*s_{7,2} term by term, whereas applying V to the rank-7 expansion s_{5,2}*s_{5,2} misses the single term s_{4,4} of s_{6,2}*s_{6,2}, the other nine terms matching term by term (the rank-7 product does contain s_{4,3} and s_{3,3,1}, whose V-images s_{5,3} and s_{4,3,1} are present at rank 8). By the threshold theorem (scaffolded separately, not used here) rank 8 is exactly |(2)|+|(2)|+2+2 for this pair, but this example only checks the finite displayed data.
items.strategy: Verification by the source's displayed products together with two independent finite checks. (a) Dimension check: at each of the six ranks n=4,...,9 the displayed multiplicities and the hook-length dimensions of the constituents satisfy sum_gamma g_gamma dim V_{gamma[n]} = (dim V_{alpha[n]})^2, with dim V_{(n-2,2)} = 2,5,9,14,20,27 for n=4,...,9; e.g. at rank 6 the left side is 1*1 + 1*10 + 2*9 + 1*5 + 1*10 + 2*16 + 1*5 = 81 = 9^2, and at rank 7 it is 1*1 + 1*20 + 2*14 + 1*6 + 1*15 + 2*35 + 1*28 + 1*14 + 1*14 = 196 = 14^2. (b) V-comparison: adding one box to the first row of each Schur function in the rank-8 expansion yields exactly the rank-9 expansion, term by term with the same coefficients; the rank-7 expansion maps to the rank-8 expansion minus the single term s_{4,4}. Both checks use only the displayed products and the definition of V.

items.title: A global product threshold is not a per-coefficient sharpness claim
items.statement: For alpha=beta=(2) the individual coefficient bar-g^{(2)}_{(2),(2)}=2 is already attained at rank 6: the rank-6 product s_{4,2}*s_{4,2} contains 2s_{4,2}, i.e. g^{(4,2)}_{(4,2),(4,2)}=2, which is the stable value bar-g^{(2)}_{(2),(2)}=2 read off from the stable row. Thus this single coefficient stops growing strictly before the whole product stabilizes: the rank-7 and rank-8 products still contain 2s_{5,2} and 2s_{6,2} respectively, matching the stable value, while the whole product is not even V-stable at rank 7 (applying V to s_{5,2}*s_{5,2} misses the term s_{4,4} occurring in s_{6,2}*s_{6,2}) and only becomes V-stable at rank 8. Therefore the exact global product threshold (the least rank from which the whole product is V-stable) is not a per-coefficient sharpness statement: single coefficients may stabilize earlier, and no claim that a coefficient first becomes stable at the global threshold is valid.
items.strategy: Verification from the source's displayed products: read the coefficient of s_{4,2} in s_{4,2}*s_{4,2} (equal to 2), the coefficients of s_{5,2} and s_{6,2} in the ranks 7 and 8 products (2 in both cases), and the stable coefficient 2s_{bullet,2} in the stable row; compare the ranks 6,7,8 products under the operator V (V of the rank-7 product equals the rank-8 product minus the single term s_{4,4}). This shows the stabilization rank of the single coefficient (2) is at most 6, strictly below the global V-stability rank 8. The counterexample does not use the general threshold theorem; it is a finite boundary witness warning against quantifying the global threshold as a sharp per-coefficient bound.
